AbstractText: Compared to the different brain signals used in BCI paradigms, the SSVEP features a high signal to noise ratio, enabling reliable and fast classification of neural activity patterns without extensive training requirements.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: In this article we present methods to further increase the ITRs of SSVEP-based BCIs.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Starting with stimulus parameter optimizations methods, we develop an improved approach for use of the Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) and analyze properties of the SSVEP when the user fixates a target and during transitions between targets.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: These transitions show a negative effect on the system's ITR which we trace back to delays and dead times of the SSVEP.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Using two classifier types adapted to continuous and transient SSVEPs and two control modes (fast feedback and fast input), we present a simulated online BCI implementation which addresses the challenges introduced by transient SSVEPs.

AbstractText.Label: SIGNIFICANCE
AbstractText.content: The resulting system reaches an average ITR of 181 Bits/min and peak ITR values of up to 295 Bits/min for individual users.

Article.ArticleTitle: Maximizing information transfer in SSVEP-based brain computer interfaces.
